Living in an apartment, I was hesitant to get any musical toy. The adjustable volume control on this keyboard is a true lifesaver! I can set it to a gentle, background-level hum for evening playtime that doesn't disturb our neighbors or our sanity. When my son is feeling more expressive during the day, he can turn it up and really 'perform' without it being painfully loud for his little sister's ears. It respects both the child's need to play and the family's need for peace. This feature alone makes it the most considerate kids' instrument we've owned.

As a music teacher and parent, I'm very picky about first instruments. This wooden keyboard has been a delightful surprise. The keys have a surprisingly pleasant, slightly weighted feel that’s so much more inviting than the cheap, plasticky toys. The sound from the speaker is clear and warm—it actually sounds like a real piano, not a harsh electronic beep. My 4-year-old was instantly drawn to it and spends ages just exploring the sounds. The rounded edges give me peace of mind when she’s playing independently. It’s the perfect bridge between a toy and a real instrument.

I've got three different sets of these, two of which are the glow kit from Vevor. The kits themselves are well equipped with many pieces, all of which very much like other brands. I did find however that some of these are rather difficult to stick into the holes. Enough so that the kids are unable to attach some of the poles into the holes where an adult is required to make the connection. This seems to be an issue for about 50% of them, but as time goes on as expected with use, it does get easier. Problem seems to like with the balls with the holes and not the rods themselves as the rods are very consistent with their extrusion. The moulds seem to have not compensated enough for material expansion during fabrication for certain areas where the sticks go in. Otherwise, they work fantastic and as expected. Even with the force applied to fasten the pieces, I have not yet broken one of the rods in 18 months of use.

My grandchildren couldn’t stop playing with it (ages 3 and 5). I would have given it a 5 but some of the holes are a little small and difficult to push all the way in making some come loose. It would be nice if it came with a small hand held auger to mildly enlarge some holes. With a little help we built a castle they could stand up in and had room for a small table and several toy chairs. The clips were helpful to hold up sheets that covered the castle.
